vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawdoc
Version: 0.11.1

The clawdoc skill bundle is a comprehensive diagnostic utility designed to analyze OpenClaw agent session logs for performance issues, cost spikes, and failure patterns. The bundle consists of a suite of shell scripts (diagnose.sh, examine.sh, prescribe.sh, etc.) that use standard POSIX tools and jq to parse local JSONL files. The logic is transparent, well-documented, and includes extensive testing fixtures. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious persistence, or unauthorized remote execution was found; the tool even includes privacy-focused features like path sanitization in its summary outputs (headline.sh). The SKILL.md instructions are strictly aligned with the stated purpose of providing automated health checks and prescriptions for agent optimization.

llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated purpose (diagnosing agent sessions) but includes scripts that read arbitrary user session directories, can write/delete files, and ship developer tooling (conversion, demo, stress generators) that could be surprising if run without inspection.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, SKILL.md and the included shell scripts all focus on parsing OpenClaw/JSONL agent session logs and producing diagnostics. Declared required binaries (jq, bash, bc) match the implementation and are proportionate to the stated goal.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts instruct the agent (or user) to run many shell scripts that read session files under ~/.openclaw and other workspace files (AGENTS, SOUL, TOOLS, MEMORY, etc.). Developer tools included (dev/convert-claude-sessions.sh, dev/run-real-sessions.sh, dev/generate-stress-fixtures.sh) will search arbitrary input directories, create output fixtures, and the converter does an rm -rf on its output directory. The repo also documents a 'self-improving' integration that writes .learnings/LEARNINGS.md. Reading session logs is expected for diagnostics, but the presence of conversion scripts that default to scanning $HOME/.claude/projects and destructive operations (rm -rf OUTPUT_DIR) is a risk if run without review.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry lists no install spec (instruction-only), but the bundle contains install.sh and many runnable scripts. That means installation is manual and not automated by the registry — good from safety perspective — but users may be prompted by README to run install.sh or `clawhub install`. Review install.sh before running. No network downloads or opaque external installers were found in the provided files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. Scripts reference optional config env vars (CLAWDOC_COST_*, CLAWDOC_MAX_FILE_SIZE) for tuning; this is reasonable for a diagnostics tool. No unexplained secret requests are present.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no registry-level persistence requested. However some scripts and README describe writing diagnostic history / learnings (e.g., .learnings/LEARNINGS.md) and test/fixture generation will write to the repo filesystem; dev scripts remove and recreate directories. These are legitimate for local tooling but worth noting because they modify disk state in user repos or home directories if executed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a legitimate session-diagnostics toolkit, but it includes developer utilities that can read many files and modify or delete output directories. Before installing or running: 1) Inspect install.sh and any scripts you plan to run (scripts/diagnose.sh, scripts/headline.sh, dev/convert-claude-sessions.sh). 2) Never run conversion or stress scripts pointed at / or at $HOME without reviewing defaults — convert-claude-sessions.sh will find files under its input dir and rm -rf its output dir. 3) Run scripts in a sandbox or on a copy of your sessions directory first (e.g., copy ~/.openclaw/agents/... to a temp dir). 4) If you want read-only diagnostics, run headline/diagnose against a copied directory and avoid demo/generate tools. 5) If you need the 'self-improving' feature, confirm where it writes (.learnings/LEARNINGS.md) and whether you are comfortable with those writes. 6) Run the test suite (make test) and inspect any side-effecting steps in the Makefile first. If you do not plan to run developer utilities, the core diagnosis scripts themselves are coherent with the skill description.
